limitations: Inferred from all n < 30000 (in-sample) and confirmed on 6,272 further n up to 2*10^7 (out of sample); no proof. The data rely on the published optimality of the split-first strategy (confirmed independently only for n <= 150).
novelty_basis: Cheigh et al. (CANT VI, Springer 2025) state that a convenient closed form for the longest game on non-Fibonacci inputs is open; no such formula found in the papers above or the OEIS (L(n) has no OEIS entry, EXP-C19-04).
statement:
Let h(k) = floor(k^2/4) and define rho_p (p = 0, 1) by rho_p(0) = 0 and, for m = F_{i+1} + t with Zeckendorf top
level i (0 <= t < F_i): rho_p(m) = r_p(i) + [i = p mod 2] * max(0, rho_p(t) - h(i-2)), where r_p(0) = 1,
r_p(i) = h(i) + 2 for i >= 1, i = p mod 2, and r_p(i) = h(i+1) + 1 otherwise. Then D(0) = 0 and
D(F_{j+1} + m) = h(j) + D(m) - rho_{j mod 2}(m) for 0 <= m < F_j, and L(n) = B(n) - D(n).
title: A two-sequence recursion for the longest Zeckendorf game on every n
